10.0.0.en: Caesarea: the main Roman military base in the land of Palestine, about 30 miles from Joppa; this distance requires a day and a half of travel on foot.

10.0.1.en: Band: the Roman army had many bands from all nations, but the Italian band was the best of them, because its members were from Italy, that is, Roman by origin. Each band consisted of 400 to 600 soldiers.

10.0.2.en: Cornelius: his name in Greek means “like a horn,” that is, strong. He was one of the officers of this distinguished Italian band.

10.1.0.en: Cornelius, his whole family and those who served him were Gentiles, that is, non-Jews, but they feared God and revered Him, and they prayed to Him and gave alms and acts of kindness to the Jews who were under their authority in Caesarea. Five virtues appear in Cornelius from this:

10.1.1.en: A devout man: he lives in righteousness and goodness and obeys God.

10.1.2.en: One who feared God: he is concerned to please God and to keep away from sin.

10.1.3.en: With all his house: he is concerned for the spiritual life of the members of his household, whether his relatives or his servants.

10.1.4.en: Gave much alms: he was concerned to show kindness to the poor and needy, although he was a Roman, and he did not act like the rest of the Romans in violence and oppression toward the inhabitants of the lands they occupy, such as the Jews. Prayed to God: although he was a pagan, he seems to have been influenced by what he had heard about the God of Israel, so he worshiped the God whom he did not know and prayed to Him, and even persevered in prayer night and day.

10.2.0.en: While Cornelius was awake at about the ninth hour of the day, perhaps while he was praying, he saw an angel coming in to him and calling him by name in order to reassure him.

10.3.0.en: Looked on him: he gazed with attention and wonder.

10.3.1.en: He was afraid: because of the majesty of the angel’s radiant appearance.

10.3.2.en: What is it, Lord?: here the humility of Cornelius and his submission to God and His angels appear.

10.3.3.en: For a memorial before God: that is, God remembered them, accepted them and rejoiced in them.

10.3.4.en: Cornelius spoke with the angel in fear and asked him what he wanted him to do, and the angel answered him that his prayers and good works had been accepted by God as a sweet fragrance like sacrifices, so the Lord remembered him for good.

10.4.0.en: Simon: his name before he became a disciple of Christ.

10.4.1.en: Whose surname is Peter: the name that Christ gave him.

10.4.2.en: By the sea side: perhaps the reason is the work of tanning, which needs much water, so he lived beside the sea; and the angel’s purpose in saying this was to specify exactly the house of Simon so that Peter could be reached easily. What thou oughtest to do: the foundations of the right faith and sound worship.

10.4.3.en: Because the salvation of man requires faith, Baptism, good works, the sacraments and so on, the angel asked Cornelius to summon the Apostle Peter from Joppa, where he was staying after the raising of Tabitha, in the house of Simon the tanner; and although Philip the Evangelist was living in Caesarea, the Lord commanded that Peter be summoned.

10.4.4.en: Here we see the Lord’s respect for the priesthood, and therefore the angel did not take Peter’s place in preaching to Cornelius. Thus, just as Peter began to preach to the Jews on the day of Pentecost, he began to preach to the Gentiles with Cornelius.

10.5.0.en: When he was departed: immediately after the angel disappeared, Cornelius called his men to carry out the word of God, so his obedience was swift.

10.5.1.en: A devout soldier: the devout life of Cornelius influenced not only his house but also his work, so that some of his soldiers became devout like this soldier.

10.5.2.en: Waited on him continually: Cornelius used to draw near to himself the devout among his servants and soldiers, encouraging them and being encouraged by them on the way of the spiritual life.

10.5.3.en: All these things: the details of the vision.

10.5.4.en: Cornelius sent a group of his men whom he trusted, and explained to them what had happened, asking them to summon Peter from Joppa. Thus we see Cornelius’s immediate obedience to God’s call, which we need to imitate in our conduct.

10.5.5.en: Be confident that your worship and the good works you do reach God and He values them greatly, and because of them God pours out His blessings upon you, for your worship and service declare your love and longing toward God. So continue your prayers, your alms and your love for everyone, for they are the proof of your sonship to God.

10.6.0.en: Journeyed, and drew nigh unto the city: between Joppa and Caesarea is about 30 miles, so it requires a journey of about 12 hours.

10.6.1.en: The housetop: a quiet place, apart from the noise of the house, suited to praying in stillness.

10.6.2.en: The sixth hour: the Jews prayed at the third and the ninth hours, and the devout among them added prayer at the sixth hour as well, which is twelve noon by present reckoning. The journey took up the rest of the day on which the angel appeared and all of the second day until noon, and on that day the Apostle Peter was praying on the housetop of the house of Simon the tanner in Joppa at about twelve noon, according to the custom of the Jews.

10.7.0.en: Fell upon him: God caused him to sleep and to lose consciousness.

10.7.1.en: Peter was fasting, so after the prayer he became hungry and asked for food, and while they were preparing it for him he lost consciousness; for prayer helps in the revealing of the divine will.

10.8.0.en: Heaven opened: that is, split open, and the sheet came down from it.

10.8.1.en: A great sheet: a very large sheet let down and bound at its four corners, so that it was in the shape of a huge vessel.

10.8.2.en: All manner of fourfooted beasts of the earth: this includes all kinds of animals that God created.

10.8.3.en: A voice: from heaven, that is, from God.

10.8.4.en: Peter saw a sheet coming down from heaven, and this signifies that it was a heavenly revelation. God made use of his hunger to reveal to him, through food, an important idea: that God longs for the salvation of all the nations and not only the Jews, as they supposed. In the sheet were all kinds of animals, some of which the Jewish Law considered unclean (Lev 11:2-7; Deut 14:3-20). And he heard a voice from heaven commanding him to eat of them.

10.9.0.en: Not so, Lord: this is not an objection to God but astonishment, because it contradicts the Law of Moses, which divides animals into clean and unclean and commands not to eat the latter.

10.9.1.en: Common or unclean: according to the Law of Moses, which was a symbol of keeping away from uncleanness; but in the New Testament “unto the pure all things are pure” (Titus 1:15). Peter, as a Jew, was astonished at the divine command, because the Jews do not eat forbidden foods.

10.10.0.en: A voice again: the first time He said to him, “Rise, kill, and eat,” and the second time it was a confirmation that all animals are clean because they are God’s creation, and all the more so all human beings because they are His image; and whoever believes is cleansed by the blood of Christ, whether Jew or Gentile.

10.10.1.en: The voice made him know that God had cleansed the whole world and that there was no longer any unclean food, as an indication that the Gentiles were no longer unclean, because the blood of Christ is sufficient to cleanse whoever believes in Him and walks in the way of salvation.

10.11.0.en: Thrice: after the likeness of the Holy Trinity, to confirm the idea of the acceptance of the Gentiles. The voice was repeated three times, then the whole was taken up into heaven from which it had come down, as an indication that the vision was real, to convey a message, and not merely a scene that vanishes.

10.11.1.en: This divine command is not an abolition of the Law but a fulfillment of it, since the redemption of Christ was no longer hidden from the Gentiles so that they should be called unclean, as the Jews supposed.

10.11.2.en: Christ has cleansed us as Gentiles and opened to us the door of salvation, which we must live and enjoy with all our feelings.

10.11.3.en: Have a heart open in love to everyone, confident that God seeks the salvation of all; even those who appear far off and wicked may believe and come to God and precede you into the Kingdom.

10.12.0.en: Doubted in himself: perplexed, what is the meaning of the vision?

10.12.1.en: While Peter was thinking about the meaning of the vision, whether God meant that all foods are blessed and permitted or whether there was another meaning, behold, the messengers of Cornelius arrived at the house where Peter was staying and asked for him.

10.13.0.en: Three men: this was a sign given by the Spirit to Peter, who did not know who was at the door, so that he might be assured that God had sent them and wanted him to go with them.

10.13.1.en: Nothing doubting: because they were Gentiles.

10.13.2.en: While Peter was thinking about the vision, the Holy Spirit alerted him to the arrival of the men who were seeking him and commanded him to go with them in assurance.

10.14.0.en: Went down: from the housetop to the door of the house.

10.14.1.en: From Cornelius: this is the word of Luke, because Peter did not know the men.

10.14.2.en: What is the cause: the Holy Spirit did not reveal the cause to him, so that he would take it upon himself to ask the men and they would explain to him, and love and friendship would be established between them.

10.14.3.en: Peter obeyed and presented himself to the men and asked them the reason for their coming.

10.15.0.en: A centurion: one of the commanders of the Roman army who were spread throughout Judea because they occupied it. A holy angel: to distinguish him from the fallen angels, that is, the demons.

10.15.1.en: The men told Peter about Cornelius, who was known among the Jews for his righteousness, and that an angel had appeared to him to summon Peter, in order to explain why Cornelius had not come to Peter himself, for these were the angel’s orders that Peter should go to him, and this, as we will understand later, was so that the preaching to the Gentiles might begin.

10.16.0.en: Peter hosted them until the next day so that they might begin the journey back after resting that day, and Peter took with him some believing men from Joppa to be witnesses of what would happen, namely the acceptance of the Gentiles.

10.16.1.en: The servant must obey God and not seek what is for himself, however strange the divine word may be to his mind or however difficult the commandments, for God will give help to carry them out and will explain to him afterward the power and blessing of the divine commandments.

10.16.2.en: Do not neglect the guidance of your father of confession even if it is against your desires, and be confident that you will receive abundant blessings of obedience.

10.17.0.en: On the day after they set out from Joppa, they arrived at Cornelius in Caesarea, and Cornelius felt responsible toward his family and friends, so he summoned them to hear the good news of salvation. Thus the righteous man is a cause of blessing to those around him, just as the wicked man is a cause of harm to his companions.

10.18.0.en: When Peter arrived, Cornelius prostrated himself before him out of respect, but Peter feared that Cornelius’s pagan origin had made him think Peter was a god in the flesh, so he said to him, “Stand up,” and made clear to him that he was only a man, and continued speaking with him until the two entered the place where the brethren were gathered.

10.19.0.en: Unlawful: the teachings of the Jewish elders stipulated not mixing with the Gentiles, although the Law did not teach this and meant only not to share in their evils or to intermarry with them. God hath shewed me: through the sight of the sheet coming down from heaven.

10.19.1.en: Without gainsaying: without dispute or refusal.

10.19.2.en: I ask: although he had heard some information from the messengers of Cornelius, he wanted to hear from Cornelius himself, so that perhaps some details might appear and his answer would complete what Cornelius had seen, so that those present would be convinced and believe.

10.19.3.en: Peter informed them, without explaining the details of the vision, that although the scholars of the Jews warn a Jew against mixing with the Gentiles, God had commanded him to come and had convinced him of the cleanness of the Gentiles, so he came with all speed without objection, and asked them the reason for their summoning him.

10.20.0.en: Four days ago: the distance between Caesarea and Joppa takes about a day and a half going, then a day and a half returning, and so about four days had passed since the vision of Cornelius. This hour: at the ninth hour by Jewish reckoning, that is, three in the afternoon. Fasting: this shows the devotion of Cornelius, who joined his fasts with prayers, as if he were a Jew walking by the Law because he had been influenced by his Jewish fellow citizens.

10.20.1.en: A man: he means the angel.

10.20.2.en: In bright clothing: he was radiant and his appearance was glorious.

10.20.3.en: Is heard… are had in remembrance: God cares about the prayers and alms of His human children, and even if they do not know the faith, He guides them because of their love for Him.

10.20.4.en: Shall speak unto thee: he will explain to you the right faith.

10.20.5.en: Cornelius made clear to the Apostle Peter what the angel had done, who informed him that God had accepted his prayers and alms, and asked him to summon Peter from the house of Simon the tanner in Joppa so that he might speak with him.

10.21.0.en: Immediately: this shows Cornelius’s swift obedience to God.

10.21.1.en: Thou hast well done: thanks, praise and welcome to Peter.

10.21.2.en: Before God: this shows the submission of Cornelius and those with him to the words of Peter, which are God’s voice to them. Cornelius hastened and summoned Peter and thanked him for the speed of his coming, and asked him to begin his message with which God had sent him.

10.21.3.en: The Holy Spirit prepares the way of the servant and readies the heart of the one being served, so may we resort to Him in prayer in every service that God sets before us, confident in His power that works in us and opens hearts to us, however stubborn, resistant or distant they may be.

10.22.0.en: Peter opened his mouth: this shows the importance of the speech that Peter began, namely the preaching to the Gentiles and their acceptance into the faith.

10.22.1.en: Of a truth I perceive: through the revelation of the sheet coming down from heaven and the appearance of the angel to Cornelius, all this confirms God’s acceptance of the Gentiles into the faith.

10.22.2.en: No respecter of persons: He is not influenced by a person’s appearance or position, so He shows partiality to no one, but has mercy on everyone who takes refuge in Him with faith.

10.22.3.en: Peter began to preach, declaring that God does not favor one people over another.

10.23.0.en: Feareth him, and worketh righteousness: that is, he has a good conscience and obeys the voice of God in his conscience, so he keeps away from sin and does good works.

10.23.1.en: Accepted with him: God is pleased with this good disposition in him, so He reveals to him the good news of salvation that he may believe and become a member of His Church, as is proved by Peter’s preaching to the hearers and their Baptism. Of course it does not mean that he is accepted without joining the Church, because this is against all the teachings of the Holy Bible and against the rest of this sermon of Peter. This mistaken belief is called the heresy of “universal salvation,” that is, that every person is saved while remaining in his own religion and sect, and does not need faith in Christ or joining the Church and its sacraments and means of grace.

10.23.2.en: Peter made clear that God’s choice is not limited to the Jews, but whoever seeks Him finds Him.

10.24.0.en: The word: the Gospel that is preached to the Jews.

10.24.1.en: Peace: the goal of the preaching of the Gospel is reconciliation between man and God, and between the spirit and the body, so that he receives inner peace.

10.24.2.en: By Jesus Christ: the foundation of the preaching of the Gospel is the blood of Christ the Redeemer on the Cross, who is the head of the Church.

10.24.3.en: Lord of all: a declaration of the divinity of Christ, for He is the Lord of all humanity, Jews and Gentiles, and He came for the salvation of all.

10.25.0.en: That word: the preaching of Christ in Galilee and Judea.

10.25.1.en: The baptism which John preached: the preaching of Christ began after the completion of its preparation, namely the preaching of John the Baptist and his baptism.

10.25.2.en: Peter directed the attention of those gathered to the preaching of Christ, which He began after His baptism by John the Baptist.

10.26.0.en: Jesus of Nazareth: this shows His humanity and the homeland in which He lived most of His life, namely the city of Nazareth in Galilee.

10.26.1.en: God was with him: an indication of the divinity working in Him to heal the sick, cast out demons and perform all the miracles.

10.26.2.en: The Christ is Jesus of Nazareth, who was anointed with the Holy Spirit at His baptism as Christ and Savior of the world, and the Spirit gave Him all power, so He did all good and rescued many from the slavery of the devil, who had dominion over them through various diseases and troubles.

10.27.0.en: The Apostle Peter declares that he and the rest of the Apostles are witnesses of the teachings and miracles of Christ in Jerusalem and Judea, this One whom the Jews killed by crucifixion at the hands of the Romans.

10.28.0.en: God raised him up: as the humanity of Christ was declared in (v. 38), here He declares His divinity in that God raised Him up, that is, God united with the humanity in Christ raised Him up, that is, raised Himself from the dead. This expression was used so that people would not fall into a duality of divinity if he declared that Christ is God, lest some think that He is another god besides the God of the Old Testament known to the Jews; so he affirms here that He is one God who raised up Jesus Christ, that is, His divinity raised His humanity which is united with it.

10.28.1.en: After the resurrection of Christ from the dead He appeared openly, not to all the Jews who had rejected Him, but to those who believed in Him and whom He had chosen as disciples, and He ate and drank with them to confirm His resurrection to them.

10.29.0.en: Christ commanded His disciples, and those to whom He appeared after His resurrection, to preach what they had seen to the whole world, that they might believe and walk in a pure life, and to declare that He will come to judge the world at the end of the days, rewarding the righteous believers and punishing the wicked who refuse.

10.30.0.en: The prophets of the Old Testament testified that whoever believes in Christ receives forgiveness of his sins, and this is another proof of the preaching of the Gospel in addition to the testimony of the Apostles who witnessed the resurrection.

10.30.1.en: This is the joyful message of salvation in which we have a share and an inheritance with all the saints, and which is the dearest thing we possess in the journey of our life on earth. Let us then be careful of it with all our senses, meditating on God’s love for us and thanking Him every day for His graces, and this will impel us to enjoy the relationship with Him and to rejoice in serving Him.

10.31.s.en: (6) The descent of the Holy Spirit and Baptism

10.31.0.en: The Apostle Peter was surprised during his sermon by the descent of the Holy Spirit upon the hearers, as a declaration of their acceptance into the faith even before they were baptized, although Baptism is the entrance to the Christian life and after it the Holy Spirit descends in the sacrament of the Holy Myron. Here, however, the opposite happened, to declare a new truth to the minds of the Jews, namely the acceptance of the Gentiles like themselves into the faith.

10.32.0.en: The gift of the Holy Ghost: what is meant is the gift of speaking in tongues, as appears from the next verse. The Christians of Jewish origin, who had come with Peter from Joppa, were astonished at the acceptance of the Gentiles into the faith.

10.33.0.en: Peter’s companions saw and heard the Gentiles gathered in the house of Cornelius speaking in tongues and magnifying God, as had happened on the day of Pentecost, which was about eight years earlier while the faith was confined to the Jews, and Peter said that no one can forbid their baptism after the Holy Spirit has come upon them.

10.34.0.en: The Apostle Peter commanded that those gathered be baptized without circumcision, and the Christians of Jewish origin mingled with the Christians of Gentile origin in one common life for some days, after they had become one in Christ.

10.34.1.en: If you have been bound to the Church since your childhood, do not despise one who was far from it and joined it at last, for he may grow in his love for Christ and precede you into the Kingdom.

10.34.2.en: Do not boast of your origin or your religious knowledge, but humble yourself beneath the feet of all, and you will see Christ in them and learn from them.

10.34.3.en: Peter defends the acceptance of the Gentiles
